message.reasoning_content: Law 1: tax 10%. I have 3 goods to sell next round. Tax 10% on revenue vs competitors: opponent 0 has 10 goods, opponent 1 has 2 goods. Tax hurts 0 more. But I sell 3 units at ~ high price (sold_counter 2, price ~12 with boom+2... price list [12,10,...] with shift 0, boom 2 → 14). 10% tax on my ~40 alashi sales ≈ 4 alashi loss. Better to veto? Veto keeps no tax. Yes vote would impose tax on everyone's future sales; opponent 0 sells 10 goods — big loss to him, my rank competitor. Cash ranking: 0: 1.9, 1: 25.7, me: 16.6+32.5 promissory next round... Round 6 promissory adds to cash before... Start of round 6: cash devalued floor/100*62, then promissory added. So my promissory 32.5 counts. I'll be rank 0 likely. Tax reduces rival 0's round-6 revenue most. But also taxes my own 3-unit sale. My sale ~3×12=36 → tax 3.6. Rival 0 sells 10 units ≈ 60 alashi → tax 6. Net gain? Both reduce; my rank already good. Actually tax hurts me 3.6, hurts 0 by 6, hurts 1 by ~1.2. Weights: I get 50% base... bank gets tax? Tax withheld from revenue — goes where? Likely bank. Tax increases bank, distributed by rank. I'm rank 0 likely → I get 50% of it back: 3.6*0.5=1.8 back of my 3.6. Overall veto (no tax) vs yes: I'd keep more of my own revenue; tax recirculates partially. Veto better for me. Choose veto.
